issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Farm constructor that initializes the animals ArrayList (students are instructed: "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments" and Main.java instantiates new Farm()). The solution repository instead provides only a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor and no no-arg constructor. This discrepancy is structural and will confuse students about which constructor to implement and may break code that uses new Farm().
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the solution and template align with the specification. Add a no-argument constructor to Farm in the solution that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) or alternatively update the problem statement and template to require and use Farm(int initialCapacity) consistently. The preferred fix is to add the no-arg constructor so code like new Farm() (as shown in Main.java) works as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument Farm constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList (students are shown using new Farm() in the template Main), but the solution provides only a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor. This creates an API/identifier mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the Farm constructor) across artifacts and will confuse students when mapping the problem requirements and template usage to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm API consistent across artifacts. Either add a no-argument constructor to the solution (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) so new Farm() works as shown in the template and as required by the problem statement, or update the problem statement and template to document and use Farm(int initialCapacity). Prefer adding the no-arg constructor (and optionally delegating to the existing constructor) to preserve the student-facing contract.
